analysis: Only scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py changed: an offline unittest that statically asserts structure of .github/workflows/ci.yml and the provider-ci-build composite action. The supplied units are the BASE text only (lines 1-799). The patch excerpt is truncated, so head-side changes are visible only as hunk fragments: new helpers (CHECKOUT/CACHE_RESTORE/CACHE_SAVE pinned SHAs, a SAVE_POLICY limiting cache saves to push on master/dev, sparse-checkout patterns, .git cache step names, without_cached_checkout/work_steps helpers), plus assertion adjustments. This is test-only code with no runtime provider path, no coordinator/provider WebSocket handling (TB-002), no key, attestation, App Attest, prefix-cache (T-041) or inference code. The visible direction is a security-neutral to positive CI hardening (pinned action SHAs, PR runs never save caches, so PRs cannot poison caches). The test continues to assert no continue-on-error, no secrets, and the required-check gate (provider-test-gate) requiring every lane, so no weakening of gating is evident in the visible base text. Limitations: the corresponding ci.yml and composite-action changes, and the head side of this test file, are not supplied, so whether the relaxed assertions (e.g. the allowed-to-fail cached checkout step, 'cache-matched-key' save policy) correspond to a real workflow weakening cannot be confirmed. The next pass should check that the ci.yml cached-.git restore step (the one step allowed to fail) is followed by a mandatory cold checkout, that cache keys are not attacker-controllable from fork PRs, and that no secrets are exposed to PR-triggered jobs. No findings are warranted from the evidence supplied.
